title: Synthetic Health Orchestrator for Private VPC Deploys: unified latency/error/saturation SLOs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) deployments currently lack a unified synthetic health layer that can measure and enforce SLOs across latency, error-rate, saturation, and token throughput. Existing probes are fragmented (node-level, container-level, and ad-hoc synthetic checks) which leads to inconsistent alerting and makes safe automated upgrades and scaling difficult for on-prem/VPC customers.

Goal: Add a Synthetic Health Orchestrator (SHO) that runs lightweight, configurable synthetic transactions from within the customer's VPC, aggregates E2E metrics (client->edge->model->response), and exports unified SLOs and burn-rate signals for latency (p50/p95/p99), request error rates (4xx/5xx), resource saturation (GPU/CPU/memory), and token throughput. The orchestrator must be deployable via our Terraform Private modules, integrate into existing rollout gates, and provide dashboards/alerting + runbook links for on-call.

Success criteria: measurable reduction in false positive alerts during upgrades, earlier detection of saturation events before customer-facing latency increases, and ability to trigger canary/rollback policies based on synthetic SLO burn-rate with <5m decision latency.
acceptance_criteria: SHO Terraform module added to terraform/modules/vpc-health with clear variables and defaults

Synthetic client runs inside VPC as a Deployment/Job (configurable frequency) and emits prometheus-compatible metrics: sho_request_latency_ms (histogram), sho_request_errors_total, sho_tokens_emitted_total, sho_saturation_signal{gpu,cpu,memory}
Central aggregator service (runtime sidecar or control-plane job) computes rolling SLO windows (5m/1h/24h) and exposes composite metrics slo_latency_p99_ms, slo_error_rate_5m, slo_token_throughput_1m
Alertmanager rules added: high error-rate (>=1% sustained 5m), latency p99 breach (>=1500ms over 5m), saturation correlated with token drop (gpu_util>85% & token_throughput_drop>20%)
Integration tests: terraform apply + e2e synthetic traffic verify metrics flow to observability stack and alerts fire in local test harness
Console display: per-VPC SHO dashboard tile with current SLOs, recent incidents, and links to relevant runbooks and PRs
Rollback/playbook: documented remediation steps and an automated canary gate that can pause upgrades when SHO burn-rate > 2x configured budget
implementation_plan: 1) Design: finalize metric schema and SLO windows (Asha + Miguel) — finish by 2025-02-13
2) IaC: create terraform/modules/vpc-health/sho module that installs a K8s Deployment + ServiceAccount + ConfigMap for probe config
3) Probe: implement lightweight synthetic client in Go (repo: infra/sho-client), supports sampling, signature-based auth, token emission, and configurable payload sizes
4) Aggregation: add runtime sidecar (or optional control-plane aggregator) to collect sho_* metrics and compute SLO aggregates, export as slo_* metrics
5) Observability: add Grafana dashboard, Prometheus rules, and Alertmanager playbooks. Wire to Console via dashboard tile and alert links
6) Tests: e2e terraform test with localkind/k3s cluster + synthetic scenarios including high-latency, error-injection, and GPU-saturation simulation
7) Rollout: staged rollout to test Private customers using canary-aware deployment (canary fraction + automatic pause if SHO triggers)
8) Docs/Runbooks: create Confluence page + runbooks + on-call checklist for SHO incidents
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Probe frequency: default 1 probe per 15s per cluster. Trade-off: higher frequency gives faster detection but increases cost and noise. We default conservative and let customers increase frequency.
Client vs edge placement: run synthetic client inside customer VPC to capture network-induced latencies. Downside: requires installation via IaC and may be affected by local maintenance windows.
Aggregation location: prefer control-plane aggregator to avoid per-cluster compute, but provide optional sidecar for air-gapped deployments where control plane cannot pull metrics.
Saturation signal: combine GPU utilization with token drop and request latency spikes to reduce false positives from transient util spikes.
Authentication: use existing VPC service account + short-lived tokens; we avoid exposing long-lived credentials in probe configs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic probes could themselves contribute to saturation during peak windows. Mitigation: default conservative probe rate and implement backoff when local utilization > threshold.
Risk: False positives from noisy networks leading to unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require correlation across multiple signals (latency+errors+tokens) before triggering an upgrade pause.

Risk: Air-gapped customers cannot reach central aggregator. Mitigation: provide an offline aggregator that writes metrics to customer's observable stack and an operator to upload aggregates when connectivity resumes.
Risk: Metric cardinality explosion across many clusters. Mitigation: limit labels (region, svc, probe-tier) and pre-aggregate on client side before exporting.
Risk: Security - synthetic client keys leaked. Mitigation: use K8s service accounts + short-lived tokens and rotate defaults during module install
testing_plan: Unit tests for sho-client (latency histograms, error counters, token counters)
Integration test: terraform apply on ephemeral k3s cluster, validate metrics scrape and alert firing
Load test: simulate sustained token throughput until saturation and validate aggregator delta detection and alert correctness
Chaos test: introduce network partitions and verify SHO false-positive protections (backoff + correlation)
Upgrade test: perform a runtime upgrade with SHO enabled and validate canary pause behavior when SHO burn-rate spikes
deployment_plan: Stage 0: internal dev environment (branch: feat/sho) — 1 week
Stage 1: staging clusters for private deployments — 2 weeks
Stage 2: pilot with 2 low-risk Private customers — 2 weeks
Stage 3: enable by default for new Private installs and opt-in for existing customers — gradual over 4 weeks
Rollback: terraform destroy module and revert runtime aggregator flag; runbook steps documented in Ops Runbook
